verdict.summary: Round 4 remains clean. The generation-keyed stateful authorization cache binds both the materialized PodStore and requested authorization model to the pinned server generation, rejects stale-cache installation after concurrent builds, and rebuilds after every published write generation. Source parsing remains fail-closed for malformed, unknown, or ambiguous selectors. Unsupported trust composition is rejected, and ODRL presence is conservatively detected before cache reuse so policy-bearing server stores cannot bypass enforcement. The focused tests are non-vacuous: they exercise the real HTTP/server-store path, warm the cache, commit an ACL update through the SPARQL writer, observe the new authorization decision, verify access-controlled querying and WAC advertisement, and cover ODRL and trust refusals. No new correctness, soundness, security, or test-validity issue is evident. Because round 3 also had no findings, progress is stagnant under the required scale.
